बॉलीवुड के नवाब सैफ अली खान को लेकर एक बेहद सनसनीखेज खबर सामने आई है! 🚨

मुंबई पुलिस ने गुरुवार को पुष्टि की है कि अभिनेता Saif Ali Khan को फोन पर एक वॉइस मैसेज के जरिए जान से मारने की धमकी मिली है। पुलिस के मुताबिक इस मैसेज में कहा गया है कि उनका भी वही अंजाम होगा जो राजनेता Baba Siddique का हुआ था।

यह धमकी Baba Siddique हत्याकांड के वांछित आरोपी Zeeshan Akhtar के नाम से भेजी गई है। मुंबई पुलिस फिलहाल इस बात की जांच कर रही है कि यह मैसेज सच में Zeeshan ने भेजा है या फिर किसी ने सेलिब्रिटीज को परेशान करने के लिए AI का इस्तेमाल किया है। 🕵️‍♂️

रिपोर्ट्स के अनुसार, हाल के हफ्तों में Amitabh Bachchan, Ayushmann Khurrana और Tusshar Kapoor जैसे कई सितारों को भी धमकियां मिल चुकी हैं। बता दें कि इसी साल जनवरी में सैफ के बांद्रा स्थित घर में भी चोरी की कोशिश के दौरान एक शख्स ने उन पर चाकू से हमला कर दिया था, जिसके बाद उनकी सर्जरी हुई थी। 😨

सितारों की सुरक्षा से जुड़ी इस बड़ी खबर और धमकियों के लिए AI के गलत इस्तेमाल पर आपकी क्या राय है? कमेंट्स में बताएं! 👇

ctx.title: Saif Ali Khan receives death threat in the name of Baba Siddique's alleged killers; police launch investigation
ctx.summary: Mumbai Police has launched an investigation after Saif Ali Khan received a voice note threatening him with ‘the same fate as Baba Siddique’.
ctx.text:
Actor Saif Ali Khan has become the latest high-profile individual from Hindi cinema to receive a death threat, the Mumbai Police confirmed on Thursday. The actor allegedly received a threat in the name of Zeeshan Akhtar, a wanted accused in the murder of politician Baba Siddique . Police have launched an investigation.
The Mumbai Police told news agency PTI on Thursday that they have started an investigation into the alleged death threat received by Saif and are verifying its authenticity. “Actor Saif Ali Khan received a voice message on his phone in the name of Zeeshan Akhtar, stating that he would meet the same fate as Baba Siddique,” a police official was quoted as saying.
The report added that police are currently investigating whether the threat genuinely originated from Akhtar or someone else is impersonating him and using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to harass celebrities.
In October 2024, Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) leader and former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique was shot dead by three assailants outside his son Zeeshan Siddique's office in Mumbai's Bandra East area.
The alleged threat to Saif's life is the latest in a series of threats made to film stars, including Amitabh Bachchan , Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor, in recent weeks. Alongside the personal threats to actors, superstar Amitabh Bachchan's Juhu residence, Jalsa, was repeatedly named in a series of hoax bomb warnings sent to authorities in Mumbai and Pune over the past month.
In October, an email sent to Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi warned off an attack on Amitabh's bungalow and singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse on November 27. Following this, Amitabh Bachchan conducted his weekly meet and greet with fans cased in bulletproof glass.
The Mumbai Police recently cracked the case involving threats to film stars like Ayushmann Khurrana and Tusshar Kapoor, concluding that a Bengaluru-based IIT graduate with no link to any gang was behind them. The police arrested 30-year-old Vaibhav Mishra, saying he used AI to issue threats. His motive remains unclear.
This is not the first time Saif has been in the news this year in connection to a threat to his life. In January, the actor was stabbed by an intruder inside his home in Bandra. Saif, 55, was hospitalised and had to undergo surgery to remove the knife fragments from his body. The accused was arrested by the Mumbai police after a few days.
The police probe has found that the incident was a burglary attempt gone wrong. Saif is married to actor Kareena Kapoor, and they have two children - Taimur and Jehangir. The entire family was in the house when the attack took place.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism.

Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day.
